tools_helpful.evidence: Bootstrapped the WinUI 3 scaffold and Windows.UI.Xaml->Microsoft.UI.Xaml rewrite; the only remaining fixes were code-level API adaptations.
session-log.txt lines 4776/4833: '[PASS] dotnet build succeeded (28 warning(s), 0 WUI analyzer warning(s))' gated the agent's done-check on a clean build.
session-log.txt line 4221 surfaced the CS0104 + XAML errors, line 4752 confirmed 'Build succeeded with 14 warning(s)'.

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP source Helpers.cs uses Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient for the connectivity/metered check
failed_apis.root_cause: The WinUI 3 SDK-style csproj sets <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>, which globally imports System.Net.Http; the unqualified 'HttpClient' in the migrated code then collides with Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient -> CS0104 ambiguous reference
failed_apis.fix: Fully qualify the WinRT type: 'Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient httpClient = new Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient();' (session-log.txt line 4305)

special_apis.special_handling: In a WinUI 3 project with ImplicitUsings enabled, WinRT types whose simple name matches a BCL type imported by the implicit global usings (HttpClient is the canonical case) must be fully qualified or aliased to avoid CS0104.

errors_encountered.error: CS0104: 'HttpClient' is an ambiguous reference between 'System.Net.Http.HttpClient' and 'Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient' (Helpers.cs 47,13 and 47,41)
errors_encountered.root_cause: ImplicitUsings=enable imports System.Net.Http globally; UWP code used the unqualified WinRT Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient

errors_encountered.error: WMC0909 'Cannot resolve DataType local:Scenario' + WMC1111 'DataTemplates containing x:Bind need a DataType' + WMC9999 internal error in MainPage.xaml
errors_encountered.root_cause: Cascade from the CS0104 failure: MarkupCompilePass2 warned WMC1509 'No LocalAssembly parameter given' because the C# compile failed, so x:Bind against the project-local Scenario type could not resolve. These XAML errors disappear once the project compiles.
errors_encountered.fix: Agent changed the ItemTemplate from x:Bind to classic Binding, but the real fix was the CS0104 correction that let the local assembly build; the x:Bind change was likely unnecessary.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Build failed with 5 errors: 2x CS0104 HttpClient + 3 XAML markup errors (WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC9999)
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 1 build-fix-rebuild cycle; resolved on the next build (line 4752)
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: ImplicitUsings/System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient collision; the XAML errors cascaded from the same failed C# compile (WMC1509 'No LocalAssembly')
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Fully qualified Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient (necessary) and switched a DataTemplate x:Bind->Binding (probably a redundant reaction to the cascade)
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md CS0104 entry for .NET-vs-WinRT simple-name collisions under ImplicitUsings (HttpClient being the canonical case) so the agent fully-qualifies the WinRT type on the first pass and recognizes the XAML errors as a cascade, not a separate defect.
